response.query: Which welfare and distributional indicators most accurately capture impacts of subsidy reform and tariff preferences on small-scale fishers, processors, and consumers?
response.answer: Welfare and distributional indicators like income levels, employment rates, and market access best capture impacts of subsidy reform and tariff preferences on small-scale fishers, processors, and consumers. These metrics directly reflect economic changes and social impacts.

results.title: The influence of new sustainable fisheries policies on seafood ...
results.content: # The influence of new sustainable fisheries policies on seafood company practices and consumer awareness in Japan. Seafood companies reluctantly change their practices in response to policy change. Consumer awareness on sustainable seafood and related policy is low in Japan. Effective fisheries policy is critical to achieving sustainable transitions in the seafood industry. Here, we present a conceptual framework demonstrating how interactions between private sector actors, seafood consumers, and new fisheries policies can influence policy effectiveness. We then apply this framework to Japan, which recently implemented two new fisheries policies to develop sustainable fisheries: the Reformed Fisheries Policy (RFP), and a policy to reduce illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing. Through interviews with companies involved in fishing tuna and importing mackerel, and surveys with seafood consumers, we investigate understandings of, opinions on, and responses to, these new policies. While the new policies led companies to change some of their operating and corporate sustainability practices, these were viewed unfavourably.
